q1.explanationZh: 女孩说骑马上山会比像他们这样步行容易（than on foot like we did），说明他们是走上去的。B 错：骑马只是他们的想法（I’d love to ride up）；A 错：攀岩的是山谷对面的人，他们自己没有攀岩。

q2.explanationZh: 女孩说街上的垃圾问题很严重，想多了解怎样防止，决定以此为题，而不选海洋垃圾（I’ll go for that as my subject rather than rubbish in the oceans）。B 错：海洋垃圾是男孩提到的；C 错：她只说回收玻璃和塑料很重要，没说要研究它。

q3.explanationZh: 女孩本来要去派对，但弟弟的作业需要帮忙（my little brother needed some help with his homework），妈妈让她去帮弟弟。C 错：她没去成派对；A 错：作业和古典音乐有关、她会拉小提琴，但她并没有说昨晚在拉琴。

q4.explanationZh: 男孩看到午餐时间有小份比萨，说就点一个（I’ll go for one of those）。C 错：他不确定自己饿到能吃下汉堡和薯条；A 错：女孩建议加沙拉，他说现在不想吃。

q5.explanationZh: 老师说那里没有咖啡馆，一定要带上午饭（make sure you have your lunch with you）。A 错：大家已经交过钱，那里也没有商店，不用带钱；B 错：球拍和饮料由网球中心提供。

q6.explanationZh: 女孩会买恐龙书；男孩不买太空书（哥哥有一本，可以借），也不买非洲野生动物的书（主要是照片、信息太少）。女孩说他要买的和她会买的一样，他说 Yes, I am，所以买恐龙书。

q7.explanationZh: 路上车太多，不适合骑车；姐姐明天要去骑车，没法开车送他们，所以只能坐有轨电车。男孩说 At least, we’ll get there quickly，呼应女孩前面说的电车很快（the tram’s pretty fast）。A、B 都被否定了。

q8.explanationZh: 男孩说那天他们是更强的一队（We were the stronger team on the day），所以赢了。A 错：他说赢球并不太意外，表现在预料之中；B 错：他们赢了（we beat them），不是差点赢。

q9.explanationZh: 女孩说接下来几周没什么她感兴趣的电影，男孩也说影院应该放大家真正想看的电影，两人都希望有更多好电影。B 错：只有男孩觉得银幕小，女孩觉得还好；C 错：影院早上已经放电影了，男孩觉得这样很好。

q10.explanationZh: 教练说一般要上三节课才能独自驾船穿过港口，而她这次就做到了，她说 It was incredible，对自己的进步感到惊讶。A 错：风很小，不适合快速航行；C 错：其他学生想让教练帮忙，她是自己独立完成的。

q11.explanationZh: 男孩说赢得一大笔奖金会改变人生，女孩说这正是她参赛的原因（That’s the reason I’m doing it）。A 错：她担心在很多人面前表演会紧张；B 错：她不确定自己想不想照片上报、被大家议论。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩说他借了一本很有新意的书，肯定女孩会喜欢（I’m sure you’d enjoy it），还会把书名发短信给她，就是在推荐一本书。C 错：书是他从图书馆借的，他没说要借给她；A 错：他没有劝她多读不同种类的书。

q13.explanationZh: 男孩说只有和朋友组队完成挑战时，这个游戏才好玩，一个人玩不值得（only if you get together with friends and do the challenges as a team）。B 错：他玩了很久还是和刚开始一样差；C 错：他说这个游戏对弟弟那个年龄段太难了。

q14.explanationZh: 老师让大家早上 8 点到停车场集合，但车要在 8 点半出发（we need to set off at half past），所以填 half past eight / eight thirty / 8.30；8 点只是集合时间。

q15.explanationZh: 老师说一定要带一个水瓶（make sure you have a bottle），可以随时装水。营地没有 wifi，不必带手机；睡袋由营地提供。

q16.explanationZh: 大家会在一个专门搭起来的帐篷里做饭、吃晚饭（we’re setting up a special tent. That’s where we’ll cook and have dinner）。营地的食堂楼装不下这么多人。

q17.explanationZh: 营地附近有一座城堡，放好行李后就去那里（There’s a castle not far from the campsite）。河流和森林只是在城堡上能看到的风景。

q18.explanationZh: 去年最后一晚是烧烤，今年考虑过知识竞赛，最后决定办一场表演（we decided on a show）。

q19.explanationZh: 老师逐个字母拼出了网址：B-R-A-K-L-E-I-G-H，网址是 www.brakleigh.trip.org。

q20.explanationZh: Karina 说即使在第一个小时她也学到了一些东西，并为自己感到骄傲（I was very proud of myself），说明她对自己的进步很满意。B 错：她提到有很多孩子，但没说为此惊讶；C 错：她觉得大孩子们很厉害，但没有为此担心。

q21.explanationZh: 她说朋友们喜欢试着做她展示的跳跃等动作（They like to have a go at the jumps and other things I show them）。C 错：他们是互相比较训练内容，没说向她请教；A 错：不同的运动和爱好让他们有学校以外的话题，没人叫她别谈体操。

q22.explanationZh: 她说最棒的是体操运动员彼此都很友好，大家都想赢，所以这是她没想到的（it’s not something I’d expect）。C 错：她说紧张是正常的，每个人都会紧张；B 错：她说犯错是每个人都会发生的事。

q23.explanationZh: 妈妈要等她做完作业才开车送她去体操馆，所以放学回家第一件事就是做作业（it’s the first thing I do when I get in from school）。A 错：有一次她把作业留到训练之后，结果太累只能去睡觉，以后再也没这样做；B 错：作业要在去体操馆之前做完。

q24.explanationZh: 她说她得和家里其他人吃不一样的饭，给父母增加了额外的工作，觉得很遗憾（It’s a shame），说明她希望能和家人吃一样的饭。C 错：她偶尔也吃甜点和蛋糕，没说想多吃；B 错：她没提想吃更多种类的菜。

q25.explanationZh: 她每天有很多事要做，需要仔细安排，她说这方面的本领要感谢体操（I can thank gymnastics for my skills there），也就是学会了合理利用时间。C 错：团队合作是她在学校学会的；A 错：她说在家帮忙做家务和体操无关。

content.v: Test Four. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now look at the instructions for Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. How did they reach the top of the mountain?
Look at that view, Dad! I’m glad we made it to the top. I wanted to give up when we got to that really difficult bit. It’d be easier to go up on the back of a horse than on foot like we did.

I know. I’d love to ride up. Did you see those guys climbing the mountain across the valley? I’ve heard you can climb it from the other side, but it’s really steep and we’d need proper climbing equipment.
Yeah – what we did was hard enough!
Two. What does the girl decide to do her project about?
Have you chosen what to focus on in your project about rubbish and the environment?
Well, I think it’s important for people to recycle glass and plastic …
Yes, and I was shocked how much rubbish ends up in the sea.

Mmm … that’s been in the news a lot recently. But rubbish in the street’s such a problem – I think I’d like to learn more about ways of stopping it. I think I’ll go for that as my subject rather than rubbish in the oceans.
Three. What did the girl do last night?
Hi, Jack. Did you go to Tom’s party last night? I heard they played fantastic music and had delicious food.
I thought you were going to come, too.
I was, but my little brother needed some help with his homework – it was all about classical music, so as I play the violin, Mum wanted me to help him.
Oh, no! It was a great party.
Yes, I was really looking forward to it. And I’d already asked if I could miss orchestra practice! I love a good party.
Four. Which food does the boy want to order?
So what would you like to eat?
Hmm, I’m not sure. They do really nice burgers here with chips, but I’m not sure I’m hungry enough for one of those.
The pizzas are good, too.
I don’t think I want a whole one, though – they’re quite big. Oh, look, it says they do small ones at lunchtimes, so I’ll go for one of those.
Do you want some salad with it?
That’d be healthy, but I don’t really feel like it right now.
OK, great. Let’s order then.
Five. What must students take to school tomorrow?

Listen, everyone. It’s our trip to the National Tennis Centre tomorrow. You’ve all paid for the trip, so there’s no need to bring any money with you, especially as there’s no shop there, so you won’t be able to get any souvenirs. There isn’t a café either, so make sure you have your lunch with you. Drinks will be provided by the Centre, as will the rackets, which is good as there isn’t really room on the bus for you all to bring your own anyway.
Six. Which book does the boy decide to buy?
I can’t decide which book to get. Which one would you buy?
I’d get the one about dinosaurs, but you need to choose what you want.

True. My brother’s already got a book about space, which I sometimes borrow, so maybe that’s not the best one to buy. The book about the wildlife of Africa looks great, but it’s mainly photos and there isn’t much information. I prefer to have more.
It looks like you’re going to buy the same one I’d get then.
Yes, I am.
Seven. How will the friends get to the skateboard park?
How are we getting to the skateboard park tomorrow?
I’d love to go by bike, but the roads are always so busy.
I know – my sister hardly ever drives into town now because of the traffic! But the tram’s pretty fast.
I wouldn’t mind going by car, though! Maybe ask her … just in case?
Well, she’s normally happy to give me a lift, but she’s going on a bike ride in the countryside tomorrow! So we haven’t got much of a choice.
At least, we’ll get there quickly.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear two friends talking about a basketball match.
I wanted to come and see your basketball match yesterday. I heard it was a good game.
Yeah, it was.
So, what happened?

Well, we knew the team we were playing against were good. But our coach told us we’d improved a lot in the last few weeks, so we were feeling pretty confident. We were the stronger team on the day, so I wasn’t really that surprised that we beat them. But to be fair, it was still a very close match. It’s a shame you missed it.
I’ll make sure I come to your next one.
Nine. You will hear two friends talking about a new cinema.
Have you been to the new cinema yet?
Yes, I saw that film Spaceworld – it was so long.
I saw that too, and I found the screen a bit small, especially if you’re at the back.
I thought it was fine. Anyway, they show several films each day, so there’s quite a choice, but there’s not much on in the next few weeks that I’m interested in, which is a shame.
I think it’s good to have films on in the morning like they do, but they need to put on things that people actually want to see.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about a sailing lesson.
How was the sailing lesson? Did you get cold?
Actually, it was a calm, sunny day on the coast – perfect for sunbathing, but not for sailing fast!
Oh!
Yeah, the wind wasn’t very strong. But I still managed to sail on my own, right across the harbour!
Wow!

I know! And the instructor explained it usually takes about three lessons before people do that! It was incredible. The other students just wanted the instructor to sail their boats, rather than trying themselves.
Oh! So you were left on your own?
Well, yeah! But actually, it was better that way!
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about a TV talent competition.
I’m applying to enter a TV talent competition.
Really?
Yes, I’m going to sing and play my guitar, but I think I’ll be really nervous. Performing in front of all those people won’t be easy.
I know. But can you imagine winning loads of cash? It’d completely change your life.

That’s the reason I’m doing it. I’ve got big plans for what to do with it. Anyway, I’ll really need to practise a lot to have a good chance. I don’t know if I’d like my picture in all the newspapers and everyone discussing whether I’m a good musician, though.
Yeah …
Twelve. You will hear a boy talking to a girl about books.
Have you been in the school library recently? They’ve got some new books – mostly science-fiction novels. You like those, don’t you?
I’ve read a couple of good ones, but I prefer stories that are more realistic.

I do too, mostly, but I thought the cover of one I saw looked interesting, so I borrowed it. I’m sure you’d enjoy it. I can’t remember the title right now, but I’ll text it to you when I get home. The story’s really original. It’s about a boy who loves music, so it’s not a typical science-fiction story.
Thirteen. You will hear two friends talking about a video game.
Have you played that video game Search yet? I’ve heard it’s complicated.
I got it the other day. I found it simple enough to understand, but my little brother really wanted to play it with his friends. It’s too hard for that age group, though.
So is it worth playing?

It’s not bad, actually, but only if you get together with friends and do the challenges as a team. That makes it sociable. It’s not worth playing on your own. I still seem to be as bad at it as I was when I started, but that doesn’t stop me playing.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a teacher telling students about a class camping trip.
OK, everyone, listen carefully, please. I’ve got some information about our class camping trip next week.

We’re going by coach, so please be in the car park at 8 a.m. on Saturday morning. We’re expecting the roads to be quite busy, so we need to set off at half past. It’s a two-hour journey, and we want to get to the campsite as early as possible.

The campsite doesn’t have wifi, so there’s really little need to bring a phone. See the list for what you should pack, but make sure you have a bottle. You’ll be able to fill it up with water whenever you need to. A sleeping bag will be provided for every student.

Everyone will eat together at the campsite, and we’re setting up a special tent. That’s where we’ll cook and have dinner. There’s a canteen building where most people eat their meals, but there won’t be room in there for a large group like us.
We’ve got an exciting visit planned. There’s a castle not far from the campsite, so we’ll go there after we’ve unpacked. From there, you’ll get a wonderful view of the river and forest below.

For the final evening’s entertainment, we had a barbeque last year, which was really fun. This time, we did think about having a quiz, as that’s always popular, but we decided on a show. We want you all to take part. So start thinking about what you’d like to do, please!

I’m sure your parents will want to see how we got on, so there’ll be some information about what we did and some photos online. They should log on to www dot brakleigh dot trip dot org, that’s B-R-A-K-L-E-I-G-H dot trip dot org. I’ll put all that on the website after the trip.
Any questions?
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a girl called Karina Wells, who is a member of a gymnastics club.
Today I’m interviewing Karina Wells, a teenager who does gymnastics at a club. Karina, when did you start gymnastics lessons?

I was four when my mum first took me to one. There were lots of children, of all different ages. The little ones were doing very basic exercises, but the older ones were doing incredible moves. I remember thinking how good they all were, but even in that first hour I learned a few things, and I was very proud of myself.
Do any of your school friends do gymnastics?

No, but some do training in other sports. We often compare the exercises we do. They like to have a go at the jumps and other things I show them – not usually very successfully! Our different sports and hobbies give us something to talk about apart from school.
Do you do gymnastics competitions?

Yes. I enjoy them. When I’m competing, I always remember that it’s normal to be nervous. Everyone is, and we don’t get too upset if we make mistakes because that happens to everyone. What’s great is how nice all the gymnasts are to one another. We’re all trying to win, so it’s not something I’d expect.
Do you have much time for homework?

No! Mum won’t drive me to the gym until I’ve finished my homework, and the gym’s too far away to walk, so it’s the first thing I do when I get in from school. Once I left it until after a session at the gymnastics club. I was just too tired, though – I needed to go to bed. I’ve never tried that again.
As a gymnast, are there some things you can’t eat?

It’s important I have the right diet, with plenty of fish and vegetables. I even have desserts and cakes from time to time. One thing I know isn’t easy for my parents is that I need to have different meals from everyone else at home. It’s a shame as I don’t like giving them that extra work.
What has gymnastics taught you – apart from how to be healthy and fit?

There’s so much to do every day, and that means careful planning, so I can thank gymnastics for my skills there. There are also skills I’ve learned at school that help with gymnastics – such as working as part of a group. I’m good at that. Mum says I do more around the house than most 14-year-olds – like putting things away. I’m pretty sure that’s nothing to do with gymnastics, though!
Thanks, Karina.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
